jobs.description: Mission Brief  The Propulsion Test Design Engineer is part of a multidisciplinary team responsible for the development and verification testing of liquid rocket engines and their subsystems. The role focuses on the design, performance, maintenance, and continuous improvement of propulsion test facilities and ground support equipment, while supporting test operations, commissioning, and troubleshooting activities. Your Role in Our Space Mission:     Plan and execute maintenance, modifications, and upgrades of propulsion test facilities to support current and future test campaigns.      Monitor, analyse, and improve the performance, reliability, and availability of facility systems through data analysis and troubleshooting.      Design, build, and commission test benches, test equipment, and facility upgrades.      Develop and improve procedures, risk assessments, and operational processes to ensure safe and efficient test operations.      Perform fault investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions on facility systems and test equipment.      Support test preparations, commissioning, test execution, and anomaly resolution in collaboration with test engineers, operators, and technicians.  Qualification Checklist     Relevant engineering qualification or engineering bachelor’s or master’s degree in the field of aerospace, mechanical engineering or similar      Hands-on experience in development or testing of complex systems, preferably involving extreme operating conditions such as cryogenic temperatures, high pressures, or high temperatures. Such experience can come from either relevant positions held, or internships, clubs, and other extra-curricular activities      Capable of designing fluid and mechanical systems from theoretical concept to realization and commissioning      Able to perform in high-stress environments, maintaining focus and concentration for long durations      Physical dexterity is required as working in confined spaces is necessary     Able to lift and carry 25kg     Fluent in English   Bonus Skills     Hands-on experience with fluid system and piping/tubing      Experience with at least one programming language (Python, Matlab, C, C#, Cobol...)      Knowledge of hazardous systems (cryogenic, flammable, explosive, or similar)

jobs.occupation: Technical Procurement Manager– Utility-scale solar and BESS
jobs.description: Do you want to lead procurement for the construction of the largest solar and battery storage projects in the Nordics? We are looking for a skilled procurement professional with a strong commercial foundation and the curiosity to understand technical solutions in depth. You are willing to dig into specifications, ask questions and work closely with engineers and suppliers to make well-informed purchasing decisions in a rapidly evolving industry. Join us and be part of an ambitious team building the energy infrastructure of tomorrow.What will you do at NYAB? As our Technical Procurement Manager, you will work at the intersection of long-term sourcing strategy and practical project delivery, leading procurement for utility-scale solar and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects. Your scope will include core components and services such as solar modules, inverters, mounting systems, transformers, batteries, subcontractors and related technical solutions. In this role, you will:     Own and develop the end-to-end procurement lifecycle, from early tendering and supplier evaluation to contracting and execution.     Lead strategic and commercial negotiations to secure competitive terms, balanced risk positions and strong contractual outcomes.     Evaluate supplier offers against technical requirements, cost, quality and delivery needs, working with engineering colleagues to clarify specifications and understand trade-offs.    Stay ahead of the market by identifying new technologies, suppliers and system solutions that strengthen our renewable energy projects and make our supply chain more resilient    Drive procurement priorities against project requirements, schedules and budgets – and make sure we deliver. You will act as our internal product owner, digging into specifications, drawings and technical documentation together with the engineering team until you know the product as well as the supplier does. About you You are a goal-oriented self-starter with the persistence to follow through and make things happen. You combine sound commercial judgment with technical curiosity and a willingness to work through details, ask questions and understand what you are buying. You remain composed during complex contractual discussions and take ownership of your commitments, combining speed with precision and going the extra mile when it matters. Along the way, you build trust with colleagues, suppliers and partners.We believe you have:     A master’s degree in engineering, preferably within electrical engineering, mechanical engineering or energy systems.     At least three years of hands-on experience in large-scale procurement projects with complex technical scopes, ideally in an EPC environment.     Experience in end-to-end sourcing, supplier management and commercial or contractual negotiations.     Strong cost awareness and the ability to manage priorities within time and budget constraints.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.     The willingness to travel internationally to meet suppliers and partners, and to visit project sites in Sweden and abroad. It is an advantage if you have:     Experience in construction, electrical systems, renewable energy or another technically complex project environment.     Experience procuring equipment or services for solar parks, BESS or related energy infrastructure.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Swedish.Why work at NYAB? NYAB's greatest strength is our drive and the pride we take in our work. We all pull in the same direction – forward. We value people for their competence and initiative, and you get the freedom to act along with the accountability that comes with it. Our entrepreneurial spirit is built on collaboration and commitment. We are a close-knit community where colleagues support one another, share knowledge and work together to find solutions when new challenges arise. You will never work alone – you will have the support of colleagues and leaders, and plenty of room to grow. We also offer:    Comprehensive health assessments     Generous wellness allowance     Parental pay supplement    Reduced working hours – (Sw: arbetstidsförkortning)    A secure pension planReady to make it happen? Apply with your CV or LinkedIn profile. We review applications on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you. Start: As agreed   Employment type: Full-time   Location: Hägersten, Stockholm

Lead a Global Engineering Team as Manager, Machine Engineering As a Manager, Machine Engineering, you will lead a team of approximately 20 machine engineers located in Karlstad, Sweden and Copenhagen, Denmark supporting some of the world's most advanced pulp mills, biomass power plants, and energy projects. In this role, you will combine people leadership, project execution, and continuous improvement to help deliver high-quality engineering solutions across Europe, South America, and Asia. You will play a key role in shaping the future of our global engineering organization while developing both people and processes to support long-term business success. If you have a strong background in machine engineering, pulp technologies, and global team leadership, you can take on a senior role coordinating machine engineering across our global organization.This position is preferably based in Karlstad, Sweden, or Copenhagen, Denmark, however, other locations in Sweden may also be considered.Your responsibilities     Lead and develop a team of machine engineers, supporting both project execution and competence development across the organization.      Ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective engineering deliverables for sales, procurement, manufacturing, construction, and commissioning activities.     Collaborate closely with the Mechanical Engineering Global Head, Engineering Excellence function, and other engineering leaders to continuously improve processes and ways of working.     Drive a unified and global approach to machine engineering while building competence, flexibility, and collaboration across the global resource pool.      Partner with internal stakeholders and external engineering companies to secure the right expertise and resources needed for successful project delivery and an excellent customer experience. Expectations for you     You hold an M.Sc. degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.     You demonstrate strong leadership, decision-making, problem-solving, and change management capabilities.     You have several years of experience within machine engineering and a proven track record in resource and team management.     You have broad knowledge of machine engineering practices, project execution, and engineering processes in an industrial environment.     You communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing. Additional language skills are a plus.     You are willing to travel internationally when business needs require it. To succeed in this role Success in this position requires a combination of strong technical expertise, people leadership, and a global mindset. You are comfortable leading through change, building trust across teams, and balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment. You know how to motivate and develop engineering talent while ensuring disciplined execution and continuous improvement.We also expect you to align with Valmet’s Leadership Principles, practical behaviours that guide how we lead, collaborate, and succeed together:     Take accountability – Act with ownership, set clear expectations, and follow through     Lead with courage – Champion change, try bold ideas, and learn quickly     Build on trust – Listen to understand, be open, and create psychological safety     Collaborate for growth – Work across boundaries, value diverse perspectives, and focus on customer value We offerYou will become part of a global Mechanical Engineering Management Team supporting the Pulp, Energy and Circularity business area. The role offers extensive collaboration with engineering leaders, project execution teams, technology units, business units, and external engineering partners around the world. You will have the opportunity to influence both strategic development and operational excellence while leading a highly capable engineering team. We offer an inspiring and challenging position with international exposure and significant opportunities for personal and professional growth. You'll work in a collaborative, global environment where innovation, sustainability, and continuous learning are valued. In addition, we provide local benefits, modern tools, and flexible ways of working that support a healthy work-life balance.Want to know more? For further information about the position please contact Tuomas Etula, Senior Manager, Mechanical Engineering, tuomas.etula@valmet.com. Please note that we do not accept applications via e-mail.  We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, please submit your application before November 27th. For positions with people leadership responsibilities in Sweden, delegated Health, Safety & Environmental (HSE) responsibilities form an integral part of the role. Relevant information will be shared and discussed during the recruitment process.We perform background checks and alcohol/drug testing for all employees in Sweden, in line with our commitment to a safe and secure workplace.  When everything works together  Valmet is where the best talent from a wide variety of backgrounds comes together. We work together with our customers throughout the entire lifecycle, delivering cutting-edge technologies and services as well as mission-critical automation and flow control solutions. Backed by more than 225 years of industrial experience and a global team of over 19,000 professionals close to customers, we are uniquely positioned to transform industries toward a regenerative tomorrow. At Valmet, diversity of thought drives innovation. We are committed to a respectful and inclusive environment, where people can be themselves and are supported to contribute at their best.

jobs.employer_name: Who Collaborating Centre For Int Drug Monitoring
jobs.description: Would you like to contribute to safer use of medicines and vaccines globally? We are looking for a Data Scientist for the Research Department at Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC). You will join a multicultural and dynamic environment with a clear focus to ensure patient safety globally.Since 1978, Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) has been dedicated to developing, supporting, and expanding the field of pharmacovigilance science and practice.As a World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre, we support work around the world to examine the potential adverse effects of medicines and vaccines and contribute to safer, more informed care of patients.We are a diverse, international group of pharmacists, physicians, data scientists, system developers, communicators, and many other professionals motivated by a deep belief that the work we do matters.About the roleResearch at UMC is a team effort. Pharmacovigilance experts, engineers, and data scientists work side by side to develop the best ideas and solutions. We are looking for a Data Scientist with excellent technical skills who thrives on collaboration. You will join a self-organising agile team where members share ideas openly, plan their work together, give each other honest feedback, and take joint ownership of outcomes.You will report to our Head of Data Science, Angnis Schmidt-May.What you will do You will help us make better use of data from different sources, the main one being our global database of adverse event reports. Your work will mostly cover the following areas:    Machine learning, natural language processing & large language models: develop methods to support signal management using data from case reports and scientific literature. You will judge carefully when and how AI can be trusted to enhance our research.    Scientific research and dissemination: design and run studies in internal and external collaborations, publish in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences.    Sharing methods and assets: make our methods and tools available to others, for example as open-source packages, documented workflows, and reusable models.    Product research: develop innovative methods and conduct exploratory research to improve UMC's products and services. You will work closely with product teams to turn research ideas into useful product features.Who you are    You are an excellent collaborator. You listen to others and build on their ideas. You share credit and lift the people around you.    You are curious and eager to grow. You seek feedback, reflect on it and act on it. You see learning and development as a lifelong part of your career.    You care about the purpose. Patient safety matters to you, and you hold yourself to high standards of scientific integrity. Must have    PhD in a quantitative field (e.g., statistics, computer science, computational linguistics, epidemiology, physics), or a master's degree and PhD-equivalent research experience    Track record of scientific work, such as peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations    Minimum of 5 years of practical experience in data science (from industry or research)    Strong Python/R skills    Fluent written and spoken EnglishNice to haveKnowledge of    best practices in software engineering    pharmacovigilance, medical terminologies (e.g., MedDRA) or experience working with health dataExperience    working on open-source code    working with cloud infrastructure    working with GenAI and agentic workflows    taking models and methods from research into production    working with user research and product development    mentoring or supervising othersUppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) is an independent, self-funded, non-profit foundation established in 1978 dedicated to safer use of medicines and vaccines. Through an agreement between the Government of Sweden and the World Health Organization (WHO), UMC operates the Programme for International Drug Monitoring, supporting over 180 member countries and regions in strengthening safety surveillance, and maintains VigiBase, the WHO global database of adverse event reports. In addition, UMC provides international standards and related digital solutions for secure exchange of pharmacovigilance data, including a global medicine and vaccine terminology for identification of medicinal products. With around 200 staff, UMC advances the science of pharmacovigilance and transforms its practice through technological innovation.UMC’s working language is English. We normally apply a probationary period to new appointments.If you have any questions regarding this position please contact the responsible manager. You will find the contact details at the end of this page.UMC follows the collective agreements between the Swedish Agency for Government Employers and Saco-S and ST. Union representatives are Malin Zaar (Saco-S) and Jessica Avasol (ST), +46 (0)18-65 60 60.

We are looking for a researcher in Psychology for a fixed-term position at the School of Behavioral, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR). The research is within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging.Subject areaThe subject area for this position is Psychology.BackgroundThe Division of Psychology at Örebro University is part of the School of Behavioural, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR), together with the Divisions of Legal Science, Criminology, and Social Work.Örebro university is now hiring a researcher within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging, with a particular focus on early life predictors of brain structural and functional connectivity in older age. The research will be conducted within the research environment LEADER (Center for Lifespan Developmental Research), which is headed by Jonas Persson, Professor in Psychology.Duties and responsibilitiesThe research duties include preprocessing and analyses of structural and functional brain imaging data obtained by magnetic resonance imaging. A particular focus will be on analysing diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) data to assess structural connectivity and brain network properties in older age and how these related to health, cognition, lifestyle and other factors in childhood and adolescence. Analyses of functional connectivity data from resting-state fMRI images and the relationship with early life predictors is also expected. The applicant will also have a leading role in dissemination of the results through international peer-reviewed publication and presentations.  QualificationsThose qualified for the appointment as a researcher are applicants who have obtained a doctoral degree or have a degree from abroad deemed to correspond to a doctoral degree.Assessment criteriaA general basis for assessment is that the applicant is able to demonstrate the personal qualities required to successfully perform the duties and responsibilities at hand; that they are able to cooperate with other members of staff; and contribute to the development of university operations.Specific personal abilities that are of great importance for the position is documented expertise in the fields of cognitive aging and brain imaging. Of particular importance is proficiency in analysing structural brain connectivity data, connectome-based modelling and tractography of diffusion-tensor imaging (DTI)/DWI data combined with a documented ability in analysing functional MRI data. Experience of working with longitudinal MRI data is also highly desirable, along with experience in working with software such as Matlab, R and SPM.InformationThis is a fixed-term full-time position for 12 months. At Örebro University, salary depends on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience.For more information about the position, contact Jonas Persson +46 19 301428, email: jonas.persson@oru.se, or Head of Unit Terese Glatz, +46 19 301205, email: terese.glatz@oru.se.At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.Örebro University actively pursues equal opportunities and gender equality as well as a work environment characterised by openness, trust and respect. We value the qualities that diversity adds to our operations.ApplicationThe application is made online. Click the button “Apply” to begin the application procedure.For the application to be complete, the following electronic documents must be included:    Covering letter, outlining how you believe you can contribute to the continued development of Örebro University    CV with a relevant description of your overall qualifications and experience    Account of research qualifications and experience    Copies of relevant course/degree certificates and references verifying eligibility and criteria metOnly documents written in Swedish, English, Norwegian and Danish can be reviewed. More information for applicants will be found on our career site:  https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/The application deadline is November 27, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!As we have already made our choices in terms of external collaboration partners and marketing efforts for this recruitment process, we decline any contact with recruitment agencies and advertisers.As directed by the National Archives of Sweden (Riksarkivet), we are required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

jobs.occupation: Lead Engineer – Electrical and Control Systems
jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your DayAs a Lead Engineer within Siemens Energy’s Modifications & Upgrades organization, you will play a key role in delivering modernization and upgrading projects for our global fleet of gas and steam turbines.You will be responsible for the technical coordination of the electrical and control system scope throughout the project lifecycle, from sales support and engineering to commissioning and customer handover. Working closely with project managers, customers, suppliers, commissioning teams, and engineering specialists, you will ensure that the technical solution is clearly defined, coordinated, and successfully executed.The role combines technical leadership, project execution, problem-solving, and customer interaction in an international environment. You will join a highly skilled and supportive team working with complex technical challenges, modern control systems, digitalization, and lifetime extension solutions for our installed fleet.How You’ll Make an Impact    Lead and coordinate the electrical and control system scope in modernization and upgrading projects.    Develop a clear technical execution plan, define deliverables and interfaces, and drive activities from planning through commissioning.    Act as a key technical interface towards customers, project management, suppliers, commissioning teams, and internal engineering functions.    Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering activities and ensure alignment between technical disciplines and project requirements.    Identify and manage technical risks, changed conditions, and complex engineering challenges throughout project execution.    Lead technical discussions and contribute to solutions that improve plant performance, reliability, availability, and sustainability.    Support modernization initiatives such as control system upgrades, system migrations, obsolescence management, digital solutions, and performance improvements.    Enable, motivate, and support project team members to achieve common goals and deliver successful project outcomes.    Contribute technical input to quotations and support the early definition of project scope, assumptions, and risks.What You Bring    A university degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Control Systems Engineering, or equivalent relevant work experience.    Several years of experience in control system engineering, electrical engineering, commissioning, technical project leadership, or modernization projects.    Experience with industrial control systems such as Siemens Energy SPPA-T3000, PCS 7, PCS neo, DCS, PLC, or equivalent automation platforms is highly meritorious.    Experience from power generation, gas turbines, steam turbines, process industries, or other complex industrial environments is advantageous.    Experience from modernization, upgrade, migration, retrofit, or obsolescence management projects is considered a strong merit.    The ability to structure and drive technical work while managing several stakeholders and priorities.    Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the confidence to represent the technical scope in customer and project meetings.    A solution-oriented, responsible, flexible, and organized approach, combined with a strong desire to learn and develop.    A collaborative leadership style and an interest in enabling and supporting colleagues across functions and cultures.    Fluency in English, both written and spoken.About the TeamYou will be part of Siemens Energy’s Modifications & Upgrades organization, which delivers modernization, upgrade, and lifetime extension solutions for the installed fleet of gas and steam turbines.Our work is performed in close collaboration with customers and colleagues across engineering, project management, sales, procurement, manufacturing, field service, and commissioning. We value technical curiosity, openness, teamwork, and continuous improvement, and we support each other in finding robust solutions to complex challenges.Our Gas Services division provides service, modernization, digitalization, and decarbonization solutions for gas turbines, steam turbines, and generators.What We Offer    A role with significant technical responsibility and the opportunity to influence projects from early definition to final delivery.    Work with advanced technology and challenging international projects in a collaborative environment.    Opportunities for professional development, continuous learning, and knowledge sharing within a skilled engineering community.Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.We can offer you employment benefits such as: reduction of working hours, advance vacation, health care allowance and an eventual possibility to a flexible working place.Who is Siemens Energy?At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. Bring more to life.Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology? At Cytiva, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.Working at Cytiva means being at the forefront of providing new solutions to transform human health. Our incredible customers undertake life-saving activities ranging from fundamental biological research to developing innovative vaccines, new medicines, and cell and gene therapies. At Cytiva you will be able to continuously improve yourself and us – working on challenges that truly matter with people that care for each other, our customers, and their patients. Take your next step to an altogether life-changing career.Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.We are seeking a highly motivated Scientist to support the development of innovative scientific imaging products and analytical workflows at Cytiva. The successful candidate will contribute to the design and user validation of new products, with a strong focus on fluorescence-based applications and imaging technologies. This role requires close collaboration with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders across international organizations.The Scientist reports to the Senior Manager, Protein Research Systems, part of the wider Protein Research R&D department, and will be an onsite role based in Uppsala, Sweden.What you'll do:    Lead and support the development of new imaging-based products and applications from concept through verification and user validation.    Design, execute, and analyse experiments, for example involving fluorescent dyes, chemiluminescence, and phosphor imaging.    Develop and optimize workflows related to electrophoresis, nucleic acid and protein analysis, and image-based quantification.    Evaluate imaging performance, sensitivity, reproducibility, and usability of new systems and applications.    Contribute to technical documentation, protocols, design reviews, and regulatory documentation as required.    Support customer and user studies to ensure products address real-world user needs, for example by leading beta-user testing.The essential requirements of the job include:    Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Biomedical Engineering, Imaging Science, or a related scientific discipline.    Strong hands-on experience with fluorescence-based detection methods and fluorophores.    Experience in applications such as Western blotting, nucleic acid gel electrophoresis, fluorescence imaging, chemiluminescence detection, phosphor imaging, multiplex multi-well plate analysis, or related workflows.    Experience with quantitative image analysis, data interpretation, and statistical evaluation of imaging performance.    Demonstrated ability to independently plan and execute complex experimental studies with limited supervision.    Experience developing, testing, and validating scientific instruments, assays, or research products.    Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively in English-speaking, cross-functional, and international teams.It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:    Knowledge of optical imaging systems, detector technologies (CCD, CMOS, sCMOS, PMT, SPAD, or related technologies), illumination systems, and image quality metrics is advantageous.    Experience with laboratory imaging systems such as gel documentation systems, fluorescence imagers, chemiluminescence imagers, phosphor imagers, microscopy systems, or multimode imaging platforms.    Familiarity with scientific image file formats and metadata standards (e.g., TIFF, JPEG, and other proprietary instrument formats).    Experience with user-cantered product development and usability testing.    Understanding of regulated development environments, quality systems, or design control processes.    Experience working with software-controlled instrumentation and digital image workflows.We’re looking for someone with a collaborative mindset who enjoys working across disciplines, functions and geographies. You are curious and innovative, with a genuine passion for scientific problem-solving and finding practical solutions to complex challenges. You bring a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work while remaining pragmatic and adaptable. With strong interpersonal and communication skills, you build productive relationships easily and thrive in a dynamic environment where you can manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.For more information, visit www.danaher.com.

jobs.occupation: Head chef to Mr.Bronck & Sallys at Sheraton Stockholm Hotel
jobs.description: Stockholm outside, a world of guests inside, and a kitchen ready for your ideas. It´s time to bring your flavour to Sheraton Stockholm.  Sheraton Stockholm has been bringing people together in the heart of the city since 1971. Today, we’re shaping our next chapter, with a major transformation, fresh energy and new places to eat, drink and connect. With Archer Hotel Management as our operator and Marriott International as our brand family, we combine an international outlook with a strong sense of place. Now we’re looking for a Head Chef to lead the food experience at Mr. Bronck, Sally’s and our room service operation. Someone with a clear culinary point of view, a head for business and the ability to build a team people want to be part of.  From dinner at Mr. Bronck to food that complements a cocktail at Sally’s or a great meal delivered upstairs, you’ll make sure every experience feels considered, consistent and right for the setting. You’ll lead the daily a la carte kitchen operation and develop seasonal menus that give each concept its own character. Taste, presentation and timing matter equally, and you know how to deliver all three when service picks up. Behind every great service is a well-run kitchen You’ll take ownership of menu costing, purchasing, stock control and staffing, keeping quality high and food waste low. You’ll turn business forecasts into smart schedules, maintain strong food safety and HACCP routines, and keep a close eye on the financial performance of the operation. Just as importantly, you’ll recruit, coach and develop your team. You set clear expectations, share your knowledge and stay approachable under pressure. Working closely with colleagues across the hotel, you’ll help create a seamless experience for our guests. A creative chef and a grounded leaderYou bring at least five years of experience in a similar leadership role in a quality restaurant or hotel kitchen. You’re confident developing menus, leading busy services and balancing culinary ambition with commercial results. You care about the details and understand how your decisions affect the whole operation. You bring structure, curiosity and high professional standards, and you enjoy finding practical solutions when plans change. Your team can count on you for direction, support and a steady presence during a demanding service. You communicate confidently in English; Swedish is a plus. An established network within the industry is also welcome. Make your mark on our next chapterThis is an opportunity to influence the food, develop your team and help shape the next chapter of an iconic Stockholm hotel. You’ll join an international, inclusive workplace with opportunities to grow within Sheraton and the wider Marriott family, alongside access to employee hotel rates around the world. We offer a permanent, full-time position with a six-month probationary period and terms covered by a collective bargaining agreement.Are you ready to bring your ideas to the table?Send us your application. We review applications and meet candidates throughout the recruitment process, so the position may be filled before the closing date. Let’s create something worth coming back for.

Mat4Green Tech AB (M4GT) is a Chalmers University spin-out based in Gothenburg. We develop and commercialise closed-loop processes for recovering and refining metals from industrial materials, with our own lab and pilot facilities in Gothenburg. We are now looking for a chemist who will take hands-on ownership of our recycling and purification work.About the roleYou will run and develop hydrometallurgical and electrochemical processes in our lab and pilot facility, from leaching and solvent extraction to electrolysis and final purification. Interviews are held on a rolling basis, so apply as soon as possible.

The Plant Coordinator supports the coordination and management of plant, vehicles, tools, and assets across operations in Sweden. The role supports asset management activities, lifecycle planning, and operational asset performance. The role supports plant availability, maintenance coordination, and efficient utilisation of company assets. The role works with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and service providers to support asset management, regulatory compliance, and commercial objectives.How this role lives our values This role supports the effective management of plant and assets by helping ensure that equipment, vehicles, and resources are available, maintained, and correctly managed throughout their lifecycle. By maintaining visibility of asset performance, availability, and compliance requirements, the role supports efficient operations and informed decision-making. Safety: Support a safe working environment by helping ensure assets, vehicles, equipment, and inspection requirements are managed in accordance with company and regulatory standards. Integrity: Support accuracy, accountability, and compliance through effective record management, asset tracking, and adherence to established processes. Teamwork: Build strong working relationships that support collaboration, communication, and coordinated asset management activities. Ownership: Take responsibility for following through on actions, resolving operational issues, and supporting the effective management of company assets. Sustainability: Support long-term value creation through responsible asset management, efficient utilisation, and sustainable lifecycle practices. Key ResponsibilitiesPlant & Asset Lifecycle Management:     Coordinate plant, vehicle, tool, and asset activities throughout the asset lifecycle, including receipt, return, allocation, and disposal in line with project requirements.     Support asset management strategies and asset replacement or upgrade planning. Maintenance & Compliance Coordination:     Coordinate planned and unplanned maintenance activities, inspections, testing requirements, and equipment compliance activities.     Maintain up-to-date asset records, tracking information, and compliance documentation, including leased and hired assets. Asset Operations & Procurement Support:     Coordinate plant movements, operational requirements, procurement activities, and supplier engagement.     Support commercial decision-making relating to plant acquisition, hire, utilisation, and cost management.     Support the procurement of fuel, spare parts, and other plant-related requirements. Sustainability & Asset Optimisation:     Support effective asset utilisation, reuse, sale, recycling, and sustainability initiatives in line with the company’s sustainability strategy. Fleet & Incident Coordination:     Coordinate fleet-related incidents, repairs, and recovery activities.    Coordinate vehicle maintenance requirements in line with applicable regional requirements. Health, Safety & Regulatory Compliance:     Support compliance with safety, environmental, sustainability, regulatory, and internal company requirements. Commercial Administration:     Support the effective management of plant and asset-related costs.     Reconcile monthly invoices and account statements relating to plant and assets. Key Requirements     3rd level qualification or equivalent experience in procurement, purchasing, commercial functions, or construction plant operations.     Experience in a similar position (typically 3 years or more).     Knowledge of plant and asset management.     Knowledge of Swedish regulatory requirements and construction industry standards.     Experience using asset management systems and tools.     Analytical skills, process awareness, and attention to detail.     Communication, relationship management, and stakeholder engagement skills.     Fluent English; Swedish language skills are advantageous.     Valid Swedish or EEA driver's licence.Skills     Plant and asset management knowledge.     Regulatory compliance knowledge.     Asset management systems knowledge.     Analytical and process management skills.     Stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.     Commercial awareness. TECHLA is a Gothenburg-based consulting company working with modern product development across software, embedded systems, cloud and DevOps.We started TECHLA with a simple idea: to build the kind of consulting company we would want to work for ourselves. We want to build long-term relationships, work with great people and create an environment where both our consultants and our clients can thrive.We believe in transparency, trust and giving people the freedom and responsibility to grow. Our consultants should feel that they are part of something, have a real influence and are rewarded for the value they create.At TECHLA, technology matters – but people matter even more. We believe the best results come from skilled people who take ownership, work closely together and genuinely care about what they deliver.We are big enough to deliver, but small enough to care.Would you like to build digital products and services that connect vehicles, customers and the people who keep vehicles on the road?TECHLA is looking for experienced full-stack developers for assignments in automotive and connected services. You’ll work in product teams developing everything from customer-facing applications to cloud-based services and integrations.The technology stack varies by assignment. It may include React and TypeScript on the frontend, with backend services built using Java and Spring Boot, C#/.NET, Node.js, Python or Go. Teams work with cloud platforms such as AWS and Azure.What you’ll work onDepending on the assignment, you may:    Design, build and maintain frontend applications using React and TypeScript    Develop backend services, APIs and integrations    Connect user-facing applications to cloud services and distributed systems    Work with microservices and event-driven architectures    Build and operate solutions on AWS or Azure    Develop automated tests and improve CI/CD, monitoring and service reliability    Contribute to technical design, code reviews and architecture discussions    Take features from requirements and design through implementation, testing and productionWhat we’re looking for    Several years of professional full-stack development experience, typically five or more    Hands-on experience developing both frontend and backend functionality    Strong frontend skills in React and TypeScript, or comparable modern web technologies    Strong backend experience in at least one relevant stack, such as Java/Spring Boot, C#/.NET, Node.js, Python or Go    Experience building APIs, integrations or distributed applications    Experience with AWS and/or Azure    A good understanding of testing, code quality and maintainable software    The ability to collaborate with colleagues across product, design and engineering    Fluent English; Swedish is a plus.    A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.It’s a plus if you have    GraphQL, Kafka or other event-streaming technologies    AWS serverless services such as Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB or SQS    Kubernetes, Docker and CI/CD    SQL and NoSQL databases    Experience from automotive, connected vehicles, telecom or other product-focused environments    Experience operating and improving production servicesThe mindset we’re looking forFor us, being a great engineer is about more than technical skills.We’re looking for people with a strong consulting mindset – people who understand that great consulting is about creating real value, taking ownership and being someone both the team and the client can rely on.You’re highly skilled at what you do, but you’re also a doer who cares about quality. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem. You take initiative, move things forward and care about delivering work you can genuinely be proud of.At the same time, you genuinely enjoy working with others. You communicate openly, share knowledge, contribute to a positive team dynamic and believe that the best results are created together.You take responsibility for the bigger picture, stay solution-oriented and aren’t afraid to go the extra mile when it makes a difference. At the same time, you’re humble, genuine and enjoy working with people who challenge and support each other.In short, we’re looking for engineers who want to go beyond – technically, professionally and as part of a team.We’re open to both employment and freelance/subcontractor setups – so whether you’re looking to join TECHLA or take on your next assignment as an independent consultant, we’d love to hear from you.Feel free to reach out to johanna.bornemyr@techla.se or submit your application, and we’ll be happy to tell you more about the opportunities.
